citation: 'Frances Glessner Lee (1878-1962)', Visible Proofs: Forensic Views of the Body, biographies gallery, U.S. National Library of Medicine.
author: U.S. National Library of Medicine
rights_note: A U.S. government exhibition page, cited in words only.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-30 (T-3250) through a fetch that returned the biography in short quoted fragments.
note: Fragments read: she 'helped to establish the Department of Legal Medicine at Harvard' (1931); she built 'a series of eighteen miniature crime-scene dioramas for student analysis', presented to Harvard's department and later passed to the Maryland Chief Medical Examiner's Office; in 1943 she was appointed a captain in the New Hampshire State Police, 'the first woman in the United States to hold such a position.'
what_it_supplies: her part in founding Harvard's Department of Legal Medicine, 1931
the eighteen miniature crime-scene dioramas and where they went
her 1943 captaincy in the New Hampshire State Police, the first woman in the US to hold such a rank
what_it_does_not_supply: the name Nutshell Studies, which the Glessner House family page gives
